## Ranking

Rationale

1.  **KCNJ11 (Rank 1):** Exhibits the highest genetic association score (
0.865) and forms the pore structure for the ATP-sensitive potassium ($\text{K}_{\text{
ATP}}$) channel. It is targeted by a widely utilized and highly validated class of approved small molecule therapeutics (e.g. sulf

onylureas).
2.  **ABCC8 (Rank 2):** Serves as the key regulatory subunit of the $\text
{K}_{\text{ATP}}$ channel complexed with KCNJ11. It holds a near-identical association
score (0.865) and has well-established, validated small-molecule approved drugs. It is ranked

slightly below KCNJ11 due to its high structural complexity as a large multi-domain protein.
3.
**GCK (Rank 3):** Glucokinase serves as the primary pancreatic beta-cell glucose sensor. It
presents an exceptional globular structural profile (AlphaFold pLDDT of 93.69) and possesses a structurally validated high-

quality binding pocket. Although GCK does not currently have approved drugs on the market, it has multiple small-molecule candidates in advanced clinical stages.
